subject: Provisioner upgrade -> control-plane latency spikes / mitigation and follow-ups
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@coremed.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@coremed.ai>
Date: 2028-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in control-plane latency after provisioner rollout

Marissa,

We saw a sharp spike in control-plane latencies across our staging VPC starting around 08:45 PT following the provisioner rolling upgrade your team ran. Token refreshes and API calls timed out for roughly 18 minutes; we started failing health checks and a few jobs were requeued.

Attached are a small set of client-side traces and a sample pod log. Can you confirm whether anything in Redwood's provisioner changes could have affected control-plane connections? We’re on schedule to go to prod next week and this is blocking our sign-off.

- Elena
Elena Park
Director, Platform Engineering | CoreMed AI

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-28T09:47:00-08:00
Subject: PROD/STG control-plane latency spike — initial triage & mitigation

Team — Elena from CoreMed reported ~18m of control-plane latency spikes tied to our provisioner rolling upgrade at ~08:45 PT. Key points from their traces: increased leader-election churn and repeated reconnect attempts from agents.

What we know so far (initial):
- Provisioner rollout v2.3.7 introduced a non-blocking reconf for sidecar leases; under certain timing windows that caused transient leader loss in the control-plane subsystem.
- On nodes with heavy agent traffic (CoreMed staging), the kube-proxy / connection re-establishment path saw queues pile up causing request latency to spike and health checks to miss.

Immediate mitigations I suggest (we should action now):
1) Pause further provisioner rollouts in us-west-2 (rollback controller sets if already in flight).
2) Apply the quick-fix that disables lease reconf during active agent reconnects (Aditya to push a hotfix patch).
3) Open a dedicated ops bridge with CoreMed and share logs.

Aditya — can you capture the control-plane GC/leader-election logs (server side) for the 08:40–09:05 window and drop them to the incident folder? Karthik — can you prepare the rollback steps and a safe window for a forced rollback if hotfix is insufficient? Neha — start drafting a customer-safe summary; we’ll share it in the bridge.

Thanks — Marissa
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@coremed.ai>, Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@coremed.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-28T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Spike in control-plane latency after provisioner rollout — mitigation & next steps

Elena / Tom — thank you for your patience. Quick update from the bridge and our mitigation work: 

What we did (timeline):
- 09:02 PT: Paused the provisioner rollout in us-west-2.
- 09:15 PT: Deployed a hotfix (disable lease reconf during reconnect window) to control-plane nodes serving CoreMed’s staging cluster.
- 09:22–09:38 PT: Observed latency return to baseline and health checks pass; no further job requeues observed.

Evidence attached: controlplane-logs-20281128.txt (server leader-election traces) and mitigation-checklist-20281128.pdf.

Next steps and asks:
- We plan a controlled rollback to v2.3.6 for affected pools if any post-mitigation anomalies appear. Karthik will schedule the rollback runway; we prefer doing that in your lower-traffic window if you agree.
- We’ve filed JIRA RI-4567 with the full triage notes and proposed code/regression fix plan: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RI-4567
- We propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow 09:00 PT to review the postmortem and finalize production rollout gating for your prod cutover. Are you available?

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll follow with a short incident summary and permanent fix ETA by end of day tomorrow.

— Marissa
Attachments: controlplane-logs-20281128.txt; mitigation-checklist-20281128.pdf
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@coremed.ai>, Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@coremed.ai>, procurement@coremed.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-29T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: provisioner upgrade / control-plane latency spike (RI-4567)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for working with us yesterday. Below is a concise post-incident summary and follow-up items; the full write-up is in the drive folder (link below).

Summary:
- Incident window: 08:45–09:03 PT, 2028-11-28.
- Impact: Control-plane request latency spikes in CoreMed staging cluster; health-check failures and a small number of job requeues (no data loss).
- Root cause: Timing regression in provisioner v2.3.7 that allowed lease reconfiguration during active agent reconnects, which in high-traffic nodes caused leader-election churn and request queuing.

What we shipped as mitigation:
- Paused rollouts and applied hotfix to disable lease reconf during reconnects (rolled at 09:15 PT).
- No further errors after 09:38 PT; we did not see recurring failures during the monitoring window.

Permanent fix & timeframe:
- Engineering has a PR ready that adds a guarded reconf path and unit / integration tests. Target ETA for deploy to staging: 2028-12-04. Production rollout will be gated on a successful canary and your sign-off.

Action items for Redwood (owner):
- Finalize and merge PR, run canary tests (Aditya / Karthik) — ETA 2028-12-04.
- Deliver a short regression test plan and canary checklist to CoreMed (Neha) — ETA 2028-11-30.
- Offer a production rollout runway that avoids CoreMed’s peak hours; we’ll coordinate schedule once you confirm.

Action items for CoreMed:
- Confirm availability for the 30-minute postmortem sync on 2028-11-30 09:00 PT or propose an alternative.
- Share any additional traces from prod-like loads if you want us to run extra validation during the canary.

Links & artifacts:
- Incident ticket: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RI-4567
- Postmortem draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-example-drive-link
- Evidence attachments: controlplane-logs-20281128.txt; mitigation-checklist-20281128.pdf

If helpful, we can also provide temporary expanded logging for your staging cluster during the canary. Let us know and we’ll provision a short-lived debug window.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
